claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children would you like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you'd like to claim Child Benefit for your 8-year-old son, Alex.

Let me ask a few more questions to check your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**Does Alex live with you, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his mother.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex lives with his mother, I have a couple of follow-up questions:

**Do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep (for example, for food, clothes, pocket money, or accommodation costs)?**

If so, roughly how much do you contribute per week or month?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards Alex's upkeep. I help with things like clothes, school supplies, and other expenses. I give about £26 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, such as his mother?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his mother isn't claiming Child Benefit for him. Nobody else is getting it for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

Just one more question to make sure I have a complete picture:

**Is Alex's mother's local council paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise your situation:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- Alex lives with his mother, not with you
- You contribute approximately £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep (clothes, school supplies, etc.)
- No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

Based on this information, I can now provide my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, **you are likely eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**. 🎉

Here's a summary of why:

- ✅ **Age requirement met**: Alex is 8 years old, which is under 16
- ✅ **UK residency**: You live in the UK
- ✅ **Financial contribution**: Although Alex doesn't live with you, you contribute approximately £26 per week towards his upkeep. This meets the requirement of contributing at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit payment (currently £25.60 per week for an only/eldest child)
- ✅ **No competing claims**: No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- ✅ **No council involvement**: The local council isn't paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance

**Next steps:**
You can apply for Child Benefit through the government's official channels. You may wish to discuss this with Alex's mother first, as only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any time. If in the future you both want to claim, you'll need to agree between yourselves, or HMRC will decide.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
